new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level generalization for Chumashan (a sketch that explicitly includes 'Island Chumash = Ysleño: Cruzeño, Roseño'): word stress usually falls on the penultimate syllable. No Cruzeño-specific stress statement was found in any opened source; Golla 2011 adds only that Island Chumash phonology 'is basically that of a Central Chumash language'.
new_statements.exceptions: 'usually' penultimate -- no exceptions specified at family level; nothing specific to Cruzeño.
new_statements.domain_note: Second-hand survey statement about the Chumashan family as a whole, resting on the Central Chumash descriptions (Applegate's Ineseño, Beeler's Barbareño, Harrington's Ventureño) and the unpublished Beeler-Klar Cruzeño sketch that Mithun cites; not verified for Cruzeño words. Accessed only as search snippets, not as a held page.
new_statements.identity_note: cruz1243 'Cruzeño' = Island Chumash (Ysleño/Isleño), with dialects Cruzeño (Santa Cruz I.), Roseño (Santa Rosa I.) and Migueleño; extinct 1915 (Fernando Librado). The only stress sentence found is Mithun's family-level generalization for Chumashan as a whole, not a Cruzeño-specific description. The open accent-marked primary data held by the project are Henshaw 1884 (Heizer 1955, vocabulary 1) for the Roseño dialect and Pinart 1878 (Heizer 1952, Chumash V/VI) for Santa Cruz and Santa Rosa Islands; the substantive Cruzeño corpus is Harrington's Librado notes, described only in the unpublished Beeler & Klar sketch.
